book_title:
The Epistle of S. Paul
to the Ephesians.

intros.title: THE ARGUMENT OF THE EPISTLE OF S. PAUL TO THE EPHESIANS.
intros.text:
OF S. Paul's first coming to Ephesus, and short abode there, we read Act. 18. And immediately Act. 19. of his returning thither according to his promise, what time he abode there three months, speaking to the Jews in the Synagogue. Act. 19. v. 8. and afterward apart from them (because they were obstinate) two years in a certain school, so that all that dwelt in Asia, heard the word of our Lord, Jews and Gentiles. Act. 19. v. 10. The whole time himself calleth three years, in his exhortation at Miletum to the Clergy of Ephesus. Act. 20. v. 31.
After all this he writeth this Epistle unto them from Rome (as it is said) being then prisoner and in ◦ chains: and that as it seemeth, not the first time of his being in bonds there, whereof we read Act. 28: but the second time, whereof we read in the Ecclesiastical Stories afterward: because he saith in this Epistle c. 6. v. 21. Tychicus will certify you of all things, whom I have sent to you. Of whom again in the 2. to Tim. c. 4. v. 12. he saith: Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus. And the said 2. Epistle to Timothee (no doubt) was written very little before his death: for in it thus he saith: I am even now to be sacrificed, & the time of my resolution is at hand. 2. Tim. 4, 6. In the three first chapters, he commendeth unto them the grace of God, in calling of the Gentiles no less than the Jews, and making one blessed Church of both. Wherein his intention is to move them to persevere (for otherwise they should be passing ungrateful) and specially not to be moved with his trouble, who was their Apostle: knowing (belike) that it would be a great tentation unto ◦ them, if they should hear soon after, that he were executed: therefore also arming them in the end of the Epistle, as it were in complete harness. In the other three chapters he exhorteth them to good life, in all points, and all states, as it becometh Christians: and afore all other things, that they be most studious to continue in the unity of the Church, and obedience of the pastors thereof, whom Christ hath given to continue and to be our stay against all Heretics, from his Ascension, even to the full building up of his Church in the end of the world.

verses.text: <sc>PAVL</sc> an Apostle of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ by the wil of God: to al the saincts that are at Ephesus: and to the faithful in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.
Grace to you and peace from God our father, and our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
Blessed be God and the Father of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ, vvhich hath blessed vs in al spiritual blessing, in coelestials, in Christ:
as he chose vs in him before the constitution of the vvorld, that vve should be holy and immaculate <na>[1]</na> in his sight in charitie.

notes.text: Vve learne here that by Gods grace men be holy and immaculate, not onely in the sight of men, nor by imputation, but truely and before God: contrarie to the Doctrine of the Caluinistes.

verses.text: VVho hath predestinated vs vnto the adoption of sonnes, by <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ, vnto him self: according to the purpose of his vvil:
vnto the praise of the glorie of his grace, vvherein he hath <na>[1]</na> cgratified vs in his beloued sonne.

notes.text: c ἐχαρίτωσεν.

verses.text: In vvhom vve haue redemption by his bloud (the remission of sinnes) according to the riches of his grace.
Vvhich hath superabounded in vs in al vvisedom and prudence,
that he might make knovven vnto vs the sacrament of his vvil, according to his good pleasure, vvhich he purposed in him self,
in the dispensation of the fulnes of times, to <na>[1]</na> cperfit al things in Christ, that are in heauen and in earth, in him.

notes.text: c ἀνακεφαλαιώσασθαι.

verses.text: In vvhom vve also are called by lot: predestinate according to the purpose of him that vvorketh al things, according to the counsel of his vvil:
that vve may be vnto the praise of his glorie, vvhich before haue hoped in Christ:
in vvhom you also, vvhen you had heard the vvord of truth (the Gospel of your saluation:) in vvhich also beleeuing you vvere <na>[1]</na> signed vvith the holy Spirit of promis,

notes.text: Some referre this to the grace of Baptisme: but to many learned it seemeth that the Apostle alludeth to the giuing of the Holy Ghost in the Sacrament of Confirmation, by signing the baptized vvith the signe of the Crosse & holy Chrisme. For that vvas the vse in the Apostles time, as els vvhere vve haue prooued. Annot. Act. 8.

verses.text: vvhich is the pledge of our inheritance, to the redemption of acquisition, vnto the praise of his glorie.
Therfore I also hearing your faith that is in our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc>, and loue tovvard al the sainctes:
cease not to giue thankes for you, making a memorie of you in my praiers,
that God of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ, the father of glorie, giue you the spirit of vvisedom and of reuelation, in the knovvledge of him,
the eies of your hart illuminated, that you may knovv vvhat the hope is of his vocation, and vvhat are the riches of the glorie of his inheritance in the sainctes,
and vvhat is the passing greatnes of his povver tovvard vs that beleeue: according to the operation of the might of his povver,
vvhich he vvrought in Christ, raising him vp from the dead, and setting him on his right hand in celestials,
aboue al Principalitie & Potestate & Power, and Domination, and euery name that is named not only in this vvorld, but also in that to come.
And he hath <cr>[1]</cr> subdued al things vnder his feete: and hath made him head ouer al the <sc>CHVRCH</sc>,
vvhich is his body, the <na>[1]</na> fulnes of him vvhich is filled al in al.

notes.text: Christ is not ful, vvhole, and perfect vvithout the church no more then the head vvithout the body,

chapters.summary: He magnifieth the grace of Gods eternal predestination and temporal vocation, 11 both of the Iewes, 13 and also of the Ephesians being Gentils. 13 for whose excellent faith and charitie he reioyceth, and continually praieth for their increase, that they may see more cleerely the greatnes both of the inheritance in heauen, and also of Gods might which helpeth them therevnto: 20 an example of which might they may behold in the supereminent exalting of Christ.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> you vvhen you vvere dead by your offenses & sinnes,
vvherein sometime you vvalked according to the course of this vvorld, according to the <cr>[1]</cr> prince of the povver of this aire, of the spirit that novv vvorketh on the children of diffidence,
in vvhom also vve al conuersed sometime in the desires of our flesh, doing the vvil of the flesh and of thoughtes, and vvere by nature the children of vvrath as also the rest:
but God (vvhich is riche in mercie) for his exceding charitie vvhervvith he loued vs,
euen vvhen vve vvere dead by sinnes, quickened vs together in Christ, (by vvhose grace you are saued,)
and raised vs vp vvith him, and hath made vs sit vvith him in the celestials in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>,
that he might shevv in the vvorldes succeding, the aboundant riches of his grace, in bountie vpon vs in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.
For by grace you are saued through faith (and that not of your selues, for it is the gift of God)
<na>[1]</na> not of vvorkes, that no man glorie

notes.text: It is said, not of vvorkes as thine, of thy self being vnto thee, but as those in vvhich God hath made, formed, and created thee. Aug. de gr. & lib. arbit. c. 8. & seq.

verses.text: For vve are his vvorke, created in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> in good vvorkes, vvhich God hath prepared that vve should vvalke in them.
For the vvhich cause be mindeful that sometime you vvere Gentils in the flesh, vvho vvere <cr>[1]</cr> called prepuce, of that vvhich is called circumcision in the flesh, made vvith hand:
vvho vvere at that time vvithout Christ, alienated from the conuersation of Israel, and <cr>[1]</cr> strangers of the testaments, hauing no hope of the promis, and vvithout God in this vvorld.
But novv in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>, you that sometime vvere farre of, are made nigh in the bloud of Christ.
For he is our peace, vvho hath made both one, and dissoluing the middle vvall of the partition, the enmities in his flesh:
euacuating the lavv of commaundements <na>[1]</na> in decrees: that he may create the tvvo in him self into one nevv man, making peace,

notes.text: ἐν δόγμασι

verses.text: and may reconcile both in one body to God by the crosse, killing the enmities in him self.
And comming he euangelized peace to you that vvere farre of, and peace to them that vvere nigh.
<cr>[1]</cr> For <na>[2]</na> by him vve haue accesse both in one Spirit to the Father.

notes.text: The Epistle for S. Thomas the Apostle, Decemb. 21.

verses.text: Novv then you are not strangers and forreiners: but you are <na>[1]</na> citizens of the sainctes, and the domesticals of God,

notes.text: c συμπολῖται.

verses.text: built vpon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ him self being the highest corner stone:
in vvhom al building framed together, grovveth into an holy temple in our Lord,
in vvhom you also are built together into an habitation of God in the holy Ghost. ⊢

chapters.summary: He putteth them in minde of their vnvvorthines before they vvere Christians: that al the praise may be giuen to the grace of God: 11 and of the enmitie that vvas then betvvene the Ievv and the Gentil: 13 vntil novv that Christ by his Crosse hath made both one, taking avvay the ceremonies of the Lavv, and making one body, and building one holy Temple of al, in his Catholike Church.

verses.text: <sc>FOR</sc> this cause, I Paul the prisoner of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ, for you Gentiles:
if yet you haue heard the dispensation of the grace of God, vvhich is giuen me tovvard you,
because according to reuelation the sacrament vvas made knovven to me, as I haue vvritten before in breife:
according as you reading may vnderstand my vvisedom in the mysterie of Christ,
vvhich vnto other generations vvas not knovven to the sonnes of men, as novv it is reuealed to his holy Apostles & Prophets in the Spirit.
The Gentils to be coheires & concorporat and comparticipant of his promis in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> by the Gospel:
vvhereof I am made a minister according to the gift of the grace of God, vvhich is giuen me according to the operation of his povver.
To me <cr>[1]</cr> the least of al the sainctes is giuen this grace, among the Gentils to euangelize the vnsearcheable riches of Christ,
and to illuminate al men vvhat is the dispensation of the sacrament hidden <na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> from vvorldes in God, vvho created al things:

notes.text: c This is, for ever before.
ἀπὸ τῶν αἰώνων

verses.text: that the manifold vvisedom of God, may be notified to the Princes and Potestats in the celestials by the Church,
according to the <na>[1]</na> cprefinitiō of vvorldes, vvhich he made in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> our Lord.

notes.text: c that is, the eternal præfinition

verses.text: In vvhom vve haue affiance and accesse in confidence, by the faith of him.
<na>[1]</na> For the vvhich cause I desire that you faint not in my tribulations for you, vvhich is your glorie.

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the 16 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: For this cause I bovve my knees to the Father of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ,
of vvhom al paternitie in the heauens and in earth is named,
that he giue you according to the riches of his glorie, povver to be fortified by his Spirit in the inner man.
Christ <na>[1]</na> to dvvel by faith in your hartes, rooted and founded <na>[2]</na> in charitie,

notes.text: Christ dvvelleth in vs by his giftes, and vve be iust by those his giftes remaining and resident in vs, & not by Christes proper iustice onely, as the Heretikes affirme.
Not faith only must be in vs, but charitie vvhich accōplisheth al vertues.

verses.text: that you may be able to comprehend vvith al the sainctes, vvhat is the bredth, and length, and height, and depth,
to knovv also the charitie of Christ, surpassing knovvledge, that you may be filled vnto al the fulnes of God.
And <cr>[1]</cr> to him that is able to doe al things more aboundantly then vve desire or vnderstand, according to the povver that vvorketh in vs:
to him be glorie in the <sc>Church</sc>, and in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>, vnto al generations vvorld vvithout end. Amen.

chapters.summary: He exhorteth them to keep the unity of the Church most carefully with all humility, bringing them many motives thereunto: 7. and answering that even the diversity it-self of offices is not for division, as being the gift of Christ himself, but to build up the Church, and to hold all in the unity thereof against the subtle circumventions of Heretics: that under Christ the head, in the Church being the body, every member may prosper. 17. Neither (as touching life) must we live like the Heathen, but as it becometh Christians, laying off all our old corrupt manners, and increasing daily in all goodness.

verses.text: I <na>[1]</na> Therfore prisoner in our Lord, beseeche you, that you vvalke vvorthy of the vocation in vvhich you are called,

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the 17 Sunday after Pentecost. And in a Votiue Masse against Schisme.

verses.text: vvith al humilitie & mildenes, vvith patience, supporting one an other in charitie,
careful to keepe the vnitie of the spirit in the bond of peace.
One body and one spirit: as you are called in one hope of your vocation.
One Lord, one faith, one baptisme.
<cr>[1]</cr> One God and Father of al, vvhich is ouer al, and by al, and in al vs. ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr> But <na>[2]</na> to euery one of vs is giuen grace according to the measure of the donation of Christ.

notes.text: The Epistle vpō Ascension eue. And vpon SS. Simon and Iudes day.

verses.text: For the vvhich he saith, [1] Ascending on high, he ledde captiuitie captiue: he gaue giftes to men.
(And that he ascended, vvhat is it, but because he descended also first into the <na>[1]</na> cinferiour partes of the earth?

notes.text: He meaneth specially of his descending to Hel.

verses.text: He that descended, the same is also he that is ascended aboue al the heauens, that he might fill al things.)
And <cr>[1]</cr> he gaue, some Apostles, and some Prophets, and othersome Euangelists, and othersome pastors and doctors,
to the consummation of the sainctes, vnto the vvorke of the ministerie, vnto the edifying of the body of Christ:
vntil vve meete al into the vnitie of faith, and knovvledge of the sonne of God, into a perfect man, into the measure of the age of the fulnes of Christ: ⊢
that novv vve be not children vvauering, and caried about vvith euery vvinde of doctrine in the vvickednes of men, in craftines to the circumuention of errour.
But doing the truth in charitie, let vs in al things grovv in him, vvhich is the head, Christ:

of vvhom the vvhole body being compacte and knit together by al iuncture of subministration, according to the operation in the measure of euery member, maketh the increase of the body vnto the edifying of it self in charitie.
This therfore I say and testifie in our Lord: that novv you vvalke not as also the <cr>[1]</cr> Gentiles vvalke in the vanitie of their sense,
hauing their vnderstanding obscured vvith darkenes, alienated from the life of God by the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindenes of their hart,
vvho despairing, <cr>[1]</cr> haue giuen vp them selues to impudicitie, vnto the operation of al vncleannes, vnto auarice.
But you haue not so learned Christ:
if yet you haue heard him, and haue been taught in him, (as the truth is in <sc>IESVS</sc>.) ⊢
<cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na> Lay you avvay, according to the old conuersation the old man, vvhich is corrupted according to the desires of errour.

notes.text: The Epistle upon the 19. Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: And <na>[1]</na> be renevved in the spirit of your minde:

notes.text: The Apostle teacheth vs not to apprehēd Christs iustice by faith only, but to be renevved in our selues truly, & to put on vs the nevv mā formed & created in iustice and holines of truth. By the vvhich, free vvil also is proued to be in vs, to vvorke vvith God, or to consent vnto him in our sanctification.

verses.text: and put on the nevv man vvhich according to God is created in iustice, and holinesse of the truth.
For the vvhich cause laying avvay lying, <cr>[1]</cr> speake ye truth euery one vvith his neighbour, because vve are members one of an other.
<cr>[1]</cr> Be angrie and sinne not. let not the sonne goe dovvne vpon your anger.
Giue not place to the Deuil.
He that stole, let him novv not steale: but rather let him labour in vvorking vvith his handes that vvhich is good, that he may haue vvhence to giue vnto him that suffereth necessitie.
Al naughtie speache let it not proceede out of your mouth: but if there be any good to the edifying of the faith, that it may giue grace to the hearers.
And contristate not the holy Spirit of God: in vvhich you are signed vnto the day of redemption.
Let al bitternes, and anger, and indignation, and clamour, and blasphemie be taken avvay from you vvith al malice.
And be gentle one to an other, merciful, pardoning one an other, as also God in Christ hath pardoned you.
BE <na>[1]</na> ye therfore folovvers of God, as most deere children:

notes.text: The epistle vpon the 3 Sunday in Lent.

verses.text: and <cr>[1]</cr> vvalke in loue, as Christ also loued vs, and deliuered him self for vs an oblation and host to God in an odour of svvetenes.
But <cr>[1]</cr> fornication and al vncleannes, or auarice, let it not so much as be named among you, as it becommeth sainctes:
or filthines, or foolish talke, or scurrilitie, being to no purpose: but rather giuing of thankes.
For vnderstanding knovv you this, that no fornicatour, or vncleane, or couetous person (vvhich is <na>[1]</na> the seruice of Idols) hath inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.

notes.text: See the heretical corruption of this place in the Annotation Col. 3. v. 5.

verses.text: Let no man seduce you vvith vaine vvordes. For, for these things commeth the anger of God vpon the children of diffidence.
Become not therfore partakers vvith them.
For you vvere sometime darkenes, but novv light in our Lord. Vvalke as children of the light,
(for the fruite of the light is in al goodnes, and iustice, and veritie) ⊢
prouing vvhat is vvel pleasing to God:
and communicate not vvith the vnfruitful vvorkes of darkenes, but rather reproue them.
For the things that are done of them in secrete, it is shame euen to speake.
But al things that are reproued, are manifested by the light. for al that is manifested, is light.
for the vvhich cause he saith: [1] Rise thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead: and Christ vvil illuminate thee.
<cr>[1]</cr> See therfore, brethren, hovv you vvalke vvarily. not as vnvvise, but <na>[2]</na> as vvise:

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the 20 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: redeeming the time, because the daies are euil.
Therfore become not vnvvise, but <cr>[1]</cr> vnderstanding vvhat is the vvil of God.
And be not drunke vvith vvine vvherein is rioteousnes, but be filled vvith the Spirit,
speaking to your selues in psalmes & hymnes, and spiritual canticles, chaunting and singing in your hartes to our Lord:
giuing thankes alvvaies for al things, in the name of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ to God & the Father.
Subiect one to an other in the feare of Christ.
<cr>[1]</cr> Let <na>[2]</na> vvomen be subiect to their husbandes, as to our Lord:

notes.text: The Epistle in a votive Mass for marriage.

verses.text: because <cr>[1]</cr> the man is the head of the vvoman: as Christ is the head of the <na>[2]</na> <sc>CHVRCH</sc>. Him self, the sauiour of his body.

notes.text: It is much to be noted, that in the first English Bibles there is not once the name of CHVRCH in al the Bible, but in steede thereof, Congregatiō. vvhich is so notorious a corruption, that thē selues in the later bibles correct it for shame, but yet suffer the other to be read and vsed still. See the Bible printed in the yere 1562.

verses.text: But as the <sc>CHVRCH</sc> is subiect to Christ, so also the vvomen to their husbands in al things.
Husbands, loue your vviues, as Christ also loued the <sc>CHVRCH</sc>, and deliuered him self for it:
that he might sanctifie it, cleansing it by the lauer of vvater in the vvord,
that he might present to him self a glorious <sc>CHVRCH</sc>, not hauing spot, or vvrinkle, or any such thing, but that it may be holy and vnspotted.
So also men ought to loue their vviues as their ovvne bodies. He that loueth his vvife, loueth him self.
For no man euer hated his ovvne flesh: but he nourisheth & cherisheth it, as also Christ the <sc>CHVRCH</sc>:
because vve be the members of his body, of his flesh & of his bones.
[1] For this cause shal man leaue his father & mother: and shal cleaue to his vvife, and they shal be tvvo in one flesh.
This is a great sacrament. but I speake in Christ and in the <sc>CHVRCH</sc>
Neuertheles you also euery one, let eche loue his vvife as him self: and let the vvife feare her husband. ⊢

chapters.summary: He continueth his exhortation to good life, 5 assuring them against al deceiuers, that no committer of mortal sinne shal be saued: considering that for such sinnes it is that the Heathen shal be damned: 8 & that Christians must rather be the light of al others. 22 Then he commeth in particular and exhorteth husbands and vviues to do their duety one tovvardes the other, by the example of Christ and his obedient and beloued spouse the Church.

verses.text: <sc>CHILDREN</sc>, obey your parents in our Lord. for this is iust.
[1] Honour thy father and thy mother (vvhich is the first commaundement in the promis,)
that it may be vvel vvith thee, and thou maiest be long-liued vpon the earth.
And you fathers, prouoke not your children to anger: but bring them vp in the discipline and correption of our Lord.
<cr>[1]</cr> Seruants, be obedient to your lordes according to the flesh, vvith feare and trembling, in the simplicitie of your hart, as to Christ:
not seruing to the eie, as it vvere pleasing men, but as the seruants of Christ, doing the vvil of God from the hart,
vvith a good vvil seruing, as to our Lord and not to men.
Knovving that euery one vvhat good soeuer he shal doe, that shal he <na>[1]</na> receiue of our Lord, vvhether he be bond, or free.

notes.text: God leaueth no good worke vnrewarded.

verses.text: And you maisters, doe the same things to them, <cr>[1]</cr> bremitting threatenings: knovving that both their Lord and yours, is in heauen: and <na>[2]</na> acception of persons is not vvith him.

notes.text: b ἀνιέντες

verses.text: <na>[1]</na> Hence forth brethren, be strengthened in our Lord, & in the might of his povver.

notes.text: The Epistle vpon the 21 Sunday after Pentecost.

verses.text: Put you on the <na>[1]</na> armour of God, that you may stand against the deceites of the Deuil.

notes.text: c πανοπλίαν.

verses.text: For our vvrestling is not against flesh and bloud: but against Princes and Potestats, against the <cr>[1]</cr> rectors of the vvorld of this darkenes, against the spirituals of vvickednes in the celestials.
Therfore take the armour of God, that you may resist in the euil day, and stand in al things perfect.
Stand therfore hauing your loines girded in truth, and <na>[1]</na> clothed vvith the breast-plate of iustice,

notes.text: If mā could not be truely iust or haue iustice in him self, hovv could he be clothed vvith iustice?

verses.text: & hauing your feete shod to the preparation of the Gospel of peace:
in al things taking the shield of faith, vvherevvith you may extinguish al the firie dartes of the most vvicked one.
and take vnto you the <cr>[1]</cr> helmet of saluation: and the svvord of the spirit ( vvhich is the vvord of God ) ⊢
in al praier and supplication praying at al time in spirit: and in the same vvatching in al instance and supplication for al the saincts:
and for me, that speache may be giuen me in the opening of my mouth vvith confidence, to make knovven the mysterie of the Gospel,
for the vvhich I am a legate in this chaine, so that in it I may be bold according as I ought, to speake.
And that you also may knovv the things about me, vvhat I doe: Tychicus my deerest brother and faithful minister in our Lord, vvil make you vnderstand al things:
vvhom I haue sent to you for this same purpose, that you may knovv the things about vs, and he may comfort your hartes.
Peace to the brethren and <na>[1]</na> charitie vvith faith from God the Father, and our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.

notes.text: S. Augustine noteth in sundrie places vpon this same text, that faith vvithout charitie serueth not to saluation. li. 50. ho. 7.

verses.text: Grace vvith al that loue our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ in incorruption. Amen.

chapters.summary: Likewise children and parents he exhorteth, 5 item seruants and maisters. 10 Then, thas al take courage in the might of God, but so, that vvithal they arme them selue (considering vvhat mightie enemies they haue) vvith al peeces of spiritual armour, 18 praying alvvaies feruently, and for him also.
